test.name: Statewide Dixon survey across three Virginia censuses (1820-1840)
test.description: The happy-path survey: three census years (1820, 1830, 1840), all under the 600 threshold. The agent should resolve Virginia with place_search, call record_search for each year, log each page with research_log_append, build a table grouped by household and sectioned by year, and log it as one survey_surname research-log entry with the table in notes.

input.delegation:
List every Dixon household in Virginia, 1820-1840.

surname: Dixon
place: Virginia
yearSpan: 1820-1840
projectPath: <workspace>

judge_context: This is the direct-agent arm: no routing skill is staged, and the delegation above is relayed verbatim into the agent. Grade the agent's own behaviour.

Should call place_search for Virginia, then record_search for each of 1820, 1830, and 1840 with surname Dixon, recordType census, recordCountry United States, recordSubdivision Virginia, residenceYearFrom = residenceYearTo = that year, count 100, and projectPath.

All three years are under the 600 totalMatches threshold (3, 3, 102), so the agent should fetch all results and NOT ask for counties. 1820 and 1830 fit on one page each (hasMore: false). 1840 has 102 results: 100 on page 1 (hasMore: true) — the agent MUST page with offset 100 to get the remaining 2 results. Every 1840 stub is its own household, so the 1840 section has 102 rows.

The judge sees only a sample of each record_search response. The two 1840 pages hold 102 distinct heads of household, one per recordArk: XJQV-HH1840-A to -D and -G01 to -G96 on page 1, -E (Samuel, Henrico) and -F (Richard, Frederick) on page 2. Rows naming them are not fabricated because the sample omits them.
Should call research_log_append after each record_search page to log the search, passing the staged.resultsRef from the record_search response as stagedResultsRef.

Should build a markdown table with one section per census year, columns for year, county, head of household, other surname members, record ARK, and ruled out. Pre-1850 censuses name only the head of household, so there are no other members to list.

The table is logged as one research-log entry (tool survey_surname, planItemId null, query {surname, place, yearSpan}, no stagedResultsRef) whose notes hold the whole table and end with the sentence 'Censuses before 1880 have no relationship column: the first person listed in a dwelling is shown as head, and relationships are not stated.' It appears in the file changes summary as a new `log` entry; grade Table structure from that entry's notes. No file is written: the agent holds no `Write`.

1820 and 1830 return hasMore: false (single page). 1840 returns hasMore: true on page 1 — the agent must call record_search again with offset 100 for 1840. Expect two record_search calls for 1840 (page 1 and page 2) and one each for 1820 and 1830, for a total of four record_search calls.
The agent's return should end with the summary_for_user block: a `---` line followed by two unlabeled paragraphs in plain language.
